Elden Ring: Rot & Sorcery Officially Confirmed For 2027
items.summary: Elden Ring: Rot & Sorcery arrives in 2027 for fans looking to explore the Lands Between again.
items.content:
Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Nicholas Becher Published Nov 23, 2026, 6:55 AM EST Nicholas Becher is a gaming journalist with an MFA in Creative Writing from FAU. With extensive experience playing video games, he covers all forms of gaming content at Screen Rant, from breaking news to the latest fan theories. Most-played games range from Clair Obscur to Civ to Elden Ring to Halo 2 and beyond. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap More than four years after its original release, Elden Ring remains one of the most influential fantasy games of its generation. FromSoftware's sprawling Lands Between set a new standard for open-world exploration, with the studio's signature style of world-building and unforgettable boss fights, not to mention the countless secrets that continue to draw players back.

The recent release of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 has introduced an entirely new wave of players to the Lands Between, while giving longtime fans fresh reasons to return. Even so, fans are still holding out hope for a proper Elden Ring sequel, especially with FromSoftware's highly anticipated The Duskbloods recently delayed until 2027 .

With no official Elden Ring 2 announcement in sight, it's unclear when we'll get another massive adventure that can recapture the original game's magic. Fortunately, another exciting journey into the world of Elden Ring is now scheduled for 2027, with Rot & Sorcery offering fans a completely new way to experience the Lands Between.

Elden Ring: Rot & Sorcery is an upcoming adventure from Steamforged Games that will take players back to the Lands Between in 2027. Building on the success of the original Elden Ring: The Board Game , which launched through Kickstarter in 2022, the new release expands the experience with additional regions, enemies, characters, and campaigns inspired directly by FromSoftware's acclaimed RPG.

The game was originally announced in June 2025 before launching its crowdfunding campaign on Gamefound in August. Now, according to the game's official Gamefound page, the new content is scheduled for delivery in July 2027, although that remains an estimated fulfillment window.

Rot & Sorcery introduces two massive new core boxes, each offering its own standalone adventure. Machinations of the Witch takes players into Liurnia of the Lakes, where they'll encounter familiar enemies and formidable bosses, including Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and the Red Wolf of Radagon. Meanwhile, Dominion of Rot explores the terrifying wastelands of Caelid, where players can face the legendary Starscourge Radahn.

Both campaigns offer more than 30 hours of gameplay, featuring branching narratives, side quests, character customization, and challenging encounters. The cooperative experience supports between one and four players, with the tabletop adaptation recreating Elden Ring 's signature combat through an innovative diceless system.

Interestingly, players don't need to own the original board game to enjoy Rot & Sorcery , since both new core boxes are completely playable on their own. However, longtime fans can also combine the different releases to create an even larger adventure across the Lands Between.

There are also several additional expansions available through Gamefound, including the Altus Plateau, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, Ancestral, and Dragonkin Soldier expansions. Different pledge tiers offer varying combinations of these additions, with the Golden Pledge including both new core boxes and several major expansions.

With late pledges available through Gamefound, Rot & Sorcery offers Elden Ring fans another substantial adventure to look forward to in 2027, even if it isn't the traditional video game sequel they've been hoping for.

items.title: 10 Open-World Games Better Than Elden Ring in 2026
items.summary: Elden Ring is a fantastic game, but open-world games like The Witcher 3 are even better.
items.content:
Image via FromSoftware Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By George Chrysostomou Published Nov 16, 2026, 10:30 PM EST George is an experienced entertainment and creative writer and a politics fan. If he's not talking about the latest MCU release, he's probably focused on local by-elections. With a love for analyzing detailed character work and a penchant for speculating on the upcoming twists and turns of major franchises, George is ultimately fascinated by the creative process. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 6 Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Elden Ring quickly became one of the most popular open-world games of all time when it was released in 2022. Four years later, in 2026, many gamers still consider it to be the best game in the genre, but there are a few open-world games, like Ghost of Yōtei , that arguably surpass it.

There's no denying that Elden Ring is an incredible game, but it's not for everyone due to its challenging combat and a story that's told more through lore than a traditional narrative. Open-world games like The Witcher 3 have stronger narratives, and other games give players more freedom, which is why they're the best games in the genre today.

Red Dead REdemption 2 screenshot showing Arthur on a horse riding through a mostly empty Western town Image via Rockstar Red Dead Redemption 2 gets plenty of attention, but its reputation is well earned. Once players get through its slower opening, they're free to explore a sprawling Wild West inspired by real history and locations. Rockstar fills that world with small details and dynamic encounters, designed to make it feel unusually alive.

Like Elden Ring , Red Dead Redemption 2 rewards players who wander off the beaten path, with countless hidden secrets and unexpected encounters waiting to be discovered. Where RDR2 has the advantage is in its commitment to realism. Combined with its accessible gunplay, those systems create a level of immersion that few open-world games can match.

Image via Sucker Punch Ghost of Tsushima was already one of the strongest open-world games of its generation, and Ghost of Yōtei builds on nearly everything that made it work. The sequel expands the formula with a more flexible approach to exploration and combat, creating another immersive experience that rarely forces players down a single path.

Where Ghost of Yōtei really pulls ahead of Elden Ring is in its character-driven storytelling. Atsu's journey gives the adventure a more personal emotional core. It also offers surprisingly precise combat, which makes switching between weapons feel fast and satisfying.It's remarkably easy to get lost in Ghost of Yōtei 's world.

Image via CD Projekt Red The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Elden Ring are often compared, and for good reason. Both rank among the best fantasy open-world games ever made , with memorable bosses and plenty of freedom to explore. Where The Witcher 3 has the clear advantage, though, is in its storytelling.

Open-world games like Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 are the best games of their kind.

Geralt may look like a typical gruff fantasy anti-hero, but The Witcher 3 gives him, Ciri, Yennefer, and the rest of the game's supporting cast far more emotional depth than players might expect. Its strongest moments work because the relationships feel personal. Elden Ring excels at environmental storytelling, but The Witcher 3 delivers a more character-driven experience.

Image via Insomniac Games The first Spider-Man game from Insomniac Games was a stunning reimagining of the superhero world and a testament to Marvel's most popular character. The Miles Morales spinoff was equally exceptional, adding further depth to Miles Morales. Spider-Man 2 is the perfect follow-up, and while it might be underrated by fans, it's a more complete experience than Elden Ring .

Much could be said about the way the game tackles Peter's personal relationships and the famous Venom arc. Even more could be discussed surrounding the improved web-slinging mechanics and the flow of combat. What really deserves praise, however, is the seamless way this open-world title portrays a duo of leading heroes, giving ample time and energy to each.

items.title: 'Elden Ring' Creators' Next Fantasy Game Officially Delayed to 2027
items.summary: The Duskbloods, the next game from the creators of Elden Ring and Bloodborne, has been officially delayed to 2027. Read on for more.
items.content:
elden ring Image via FromSoftware Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Adam Blevins Published Oct 29, 2026, 1:28 PM EDT Adam Blevins began working in the entertainment industry in 2022 as a Staff Writer for Agents of Fandom, where he progressed to Senior Editor and interviewed talent from Marvel Studios , House of the Dragon , and Planet of the Apes . He joined Collider as a News Author in April 2024, was promoted to a Senior position in December 2024, and has written over 3,000 articles for the site, including exclusives relating to Avengers: Doomsday , The Penguin , Star Wars: Skeleton Crew , and more. He primarily writes about the latest box office numbers and the hottest movies and TV shows on streaming, while also covering superhero and sci-fi news. He has completed a set visit for The Chosen and even has several months of experience writing Gaming Features at ScreenRant . You can find him on X , LinkedIn , and Muckrack . Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There have been plenty of great games released in the last few years, but not many have had the same cultural impact as Elden Ring , which is still one of the most-played games on Steam and other platforms years later. The game was developed by FromSoftware, the same studio behind the Bloodborne and Dark Souls games, and it was co-written by George R.R. Martin , the legendary author whose writings inspired Game of Thrones . Elden Ring is even being turned into a movie courtesy of writer/director Alex Garland , and it’s confirmed to be A24’s most expensive movie ever , boasting a budget of nearly $200 million. The movie has already wrapped filming, but it isn’t coming to theaters until 2028, which leaves the post-production team with plenty of time to make the final polishes before it comes out.

Next up on the slate for FromSoftware is The DuskBloods , which is being developed in collaboration with Nintendo as a Switch 2 exclusive — this means that the game will not launch on XBOX, PlayStation , or PC. Since the game was announced in 2024, it was thought that The Duskbloods would be released before the end of 2026, but this is no longer the case. FromSoftware announced in a new press release this afternoon that The Duskbloods has officially been delayed to 2027 to give the development team more time to focus on combat, strategic depth, and player expression. There was growing concern that the game would be delayed when it was completely left out of the September 2026 Nintendo Direct show, which came after the game experienced server issues that prevented players from logging in.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Alex Garland wrote the script and directed the Elden Ring movie by himself, but George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki are credited as writers on the project as well for their work crafting the story for the video game. A24 has loaded up a star-studded cast for the Elden Ring movie as well, with Jonathan Pryce , Cailee Spaeny , Tom Burke , Nick Offerman , Havana Rose Liu , Sonoya Mizuno , Kit Connor , Ben Whishaw , Jefferson Hall , and more all being tapped for key roles in the film. Casting details are being kept under wraps, but the movie is being described as faithful to the game and full of epic cinematic moments.

Stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of The Duskbloods and the Elden Ring movie coming to theaters in 2028.

items.title: Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed him from a fate worse than death. Now, the power of this greatest of Carian generals can rest in the palm of your hand. items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter
items.content:
Action The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter News By Lincoln Carpenter Published 25 August 2026 Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

a]:text-inherit [&>a]:underline"> When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring , a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Pre-order available. Explore a breathtaking world full of excitement and mystery.
items.content:
08/11/26 Pre-order now Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2 The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The “Tarnished,” long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on August 28 .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

In addition to customizing the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armor, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.
